messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Memory
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Memory
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers
  - Memory → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory → Threat
  - Memory → Negative Appraisals
  - Memory → Triggers
  - Threat → Memory
  - Threat → Negative Appraisals
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Memory
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Negative Appraisals
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Triggers
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Threat

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Karan is a 41-year-old South Asian male who works as a park ranger in a national forest. He has been married for over a decade and describes his relationship with his wife as supportive but strained by the effects of his trauma. Karan was held captive during a military operation several years ago, an experience that has left deep psychological scars. Karan's traumatic event involved being confined in a small room without food or water for days. He was interrogated relentlessly by authority figures and felt completely helpless. The physical pain he endured, coupled with the constant fear of what might happen next, has imprinted vivid images in his mind—snapshot memories that return unbidden. When military topics are discussed at home or at work, Karan finds himself transported back to those moments of confinement. He recalls the cold floor beneath him and the sharp, searing pain in his wrists from being restrained. These triggers not only evoke painful memories but also reinforce a sense of isolation and humiliation that haunts him. He feels permanently marked by what happened, believing that no one else could have survived such an ordeal. The memory of those moments is so vivid that he often relives them as flashbacks, feeling the same physical pain and emotional numbness. This cycle of remembering triggers his negative appraisals, making it nearly impossible for him to trust anyone or feel safe. He has come to believe that he is set apart from others because of what happened to him. Karan’s attempts to cope with these overwhelming memories include strict control over his eating habits and imagining revenge against those responsible for his captivity. These maladaptive strategies stem from the belief that he must remain in control and protect himself at all costs. However, these behaviors also contribute to his sense of isolation and humiliation, as he feels like a failure when others suggest he should move past what happened. The physical pain he experiences during flashbacks is so intense that it triggers additional negative appraisals. He believes that the pain serves as a constant reminder of his helplessness and reinforces his belief that no one else could have endured such an experience. This cycle tightens, with each memory deepening his conviction that he is different from others. Karan’s daily work in the forest has become increasingly challenging. Being seen by other rangers or encountering authority figures in uniform triggers painful memories and intense reactions. He finds himself startled at unexpected movements, reacting as if they pose a real threat. These reactions have strained his relationships with colleagues who are unaware of his history. The combination of flashbacks and startle responses has led Karan to withdraw from social interactions both at work and at home. He pleases others by going along with their wishes, believing it keeps him safe. However, this people-pleasing behavior only serves to reinforce his feelings of isolation and humiliation. Karan's situation has become untenable. His wife has noticed significant changes in his eating habits and demeanor, which have affected the quality of their relationship. The cumulative strain of these symptoms finally pushed Karan to seek help. He is most afraid that he will never be able to trust anyone again or fully heal from what happened. Yet, there is a glimmer of hope—Karan is determined to regain control over his life and find a way to integrate his traumatic memories without them overwhelming him. In the end, Karan’s journey to recovery involves confronting not only the vivid snapshot memories but also the negative appraisals that have become intertwined with his daily experiences. He hopes to break free from the cycle of maladaptive strategies and reclaim a sense of trust and connection with others.
